last_action: DEPENDENCY AUDIT: 30 VULNERABILITIES (2 CRITICAL, 18 HIGH, 9 MODERATE, 1 LOW) DOWN TO 17 (0 CRITICAL, 9 HIGH, 8 MODERATE) VIA TARGETED OVERRIDES, NO SDK MOVE (D6). The count is not the point. The working assumption was that every advisory was build-time tooling absent from the IPA; that was CHECKED rather than believed, by exporting the iOS bundle with source maps and reading the 1,722-module list, and it was NOT QUITE TRUE. nanoid/non-secure SHIPS — a HIGH, reached from @react-navigation/routers and expo-router for route keys — and so do decode-uri-component, query-string, five @react-navigation packages and expo-router. Neither nanoid call site passes an attacker-controlled size so it was not exploitable, but not-exploitable and not-shipped are different claims and only the second was being made. nanoid taken 3.3.12 -> 3.3.18 in-major. Everything else (tar, shell-quote, undici, ws, metro*, image-size, browserslist, js-yaml, fast-uri, form-data, brace-expansion, postcss, @xmldom/xmldom, @babel/core) CONFIRMED ABSENT from the bundle. Overrides use the "pkg@range" key form where a package is installed at several majors at once, because only an in-major bump is API-safe: brace-expansion@5 exports {expand} where @1 exports the function, so a blanket ^5 would have broken minimatch@3 across the build toolchain. The remaining 17 are two upstream dead ends with no fixed release to move to — image-size (9 highs; advisories cover <=2.0.2, which is the latest publish; metro pins it and the whole metro/@expo/expo chain hangs off it) and decode-uri-component (8 moderates; 0.5.0 is fixed but ESM-only and query-string@7 requires() it, so forcing it breaks deep-link parsing in the shipped app). Both documented next to the overrides in package.json. Verified: tsc clean, 21 suites / 239 tests, expo export --platform ios builds, and expo start smoke-tested because ws sits under both Metro and the dev-client inspector — both websockets complete a 101 handshake and the dev server serves a 1,073-module bundle. ALSO CORRECTED THE STALE CLAIM in STATUS.md that all audit warnings were cleared; true in 2026-06, untrue for months, and it misdirected today’s work before the numbers contradicted it. FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-08): FIXED THE FLAKY you.test.tsx REMINDER TEST, and it was NOT the timing race it looked like. syncReminders returns early on an empty garden, Seed adds the plant in an effect, and mount() only waits on YOUR GARDEN which renders either way — so flipping the toggle before the plant landed scheduled nothing and the assertion was correct to fail. Fix: wait for "1 plant" first, as the backup tests in the same file already do. Established by measurement rather than by reading the shape — the move-the-assertion-into-waitFor fix the shape suggested still failed 3 runs in 20; with the guard, 0 in 25.

blockers.description: The watering reminder — the feature the whole app exists for — has never fired on real hardware. Everything around it is tested; delivery itself is not. Build 55b80f8a makes it observable.

iOS preview build 55b80f8a expires 2026-09-13. It is the only installable copy carrying photo-covers and plant deletion; after expiry a new build must be cut before the app can be used on the phone at all.

GitHub Actions was last seen failing on account billing rather than on code — a job ran one second with no steps, annotated with failed payments or a spending limit. Not re-verified since. CI cannot be trusted green or red until Settings -> Billing & plans is checked.
